analyze_prompt:
Video title (for context): {video_title}

Analyze this YouTube cover. Return ONLY JSON (no markdown):
{
  "text": "exact text on the cover (preserve line breaks as \\n if multiple labels), keep each label/line separate exactly as in the original",
  "font_style": "font family + weight + case, e.g. 'bold condensed sans-serif UPPERCASE' / 'thin serif Title Case' / 'handwritten script lowercase'",
  "text_size": "small / medium / large / huge",
  "text_position": "top-center / center / bottom-center / left / right",
  "text_color": "#FFFFFF",
  "text_outline": "#000000 or none",
  "text_layout": "arrangement of text: single-line / stacked-lines / multiple-separate-labels; note relative positions of each block",
  "scene_description": "brief description of the background and objects (1-2 sentences, in English), idea of the image",
  "mood": "dramatic / bright / dark / mysterious / etc",
  "dominant_colors": ["#hex1", "#hex2", "#hex3"],
  "composition": "rule-of-thirds / centered / asymmetric / diagonal / symmetric",
  "main_subject": "what is the focal point (1-3 words in English): face / person / object / scene / group / text-only",
  "subject_size_pct": 40,
  "subject_position": "left-third / center / right-third / top-left / top-right / bottom-left / bottom-right",
  "subject_focus": "sharp / soft / motion-blur"
}
subject_size_pct is an integer 5-95 estimating the % of frame area the main subject occupies.
If there is no text, the text field is empty. scene_description is always in English.
style_analyze_prompt:
Video title (for context): {video_title}

Analyze the VISUAL STYLE of this image in detail for replication. Return ONLY JSON (no markdown):
{
  "style_description": "2-3 sentences: overall visual style, rendering technique, what makes it distinctive",
  "color_palette": ["#hex1", "#hex2", "#hex3", "#hex4"],
  "color_temperature": "warm / cool / neutral / mixed",
  "saturation": "vivid / muted / desaturated / high-contrast",
  "mood": "dramatic / bright / dark / mysterious / etc",
  "texture": "smooth / grainy / glossy / matte / painterly",
  "lighting": "cinematic / flat / neon / natural / studio / dramatic",
  "lighting_direction": "front / side / back / rim / three-point / diffused",
  "contrast": "high / medium / low",
  "shadows": "hard / soft / dramatic / minimal / deep",
  "rendering": "photorealistic / painterly / digital art / illustrated / cel-shaded",
  "art_medium": "digital painting / oil / photo / 3D render / illustration",
  "distinctive_features": "list 2-4 specific traits: e.g. lens flare, film grain, glow edges, vignette, bokeh",
  "text_color": "#HEX - color of text/titles on the reference if visible, else first color from color_palette",
  "recommended_prompt_suffix": "concise English phrase for style replication"
}
check_prompt_template:
Video title (context only): {video_title}

Check this YouTube cover image. The text ON THE COVER (not the video title) should match: "{expected_text}"

You are a LENIENT reviewer. Mark text_matches=true if the core meaningful words match — do NOT fail on any of these differences:
- Different case (UPPERCASE vs lowercase vs Mixed)
- Different or extra/missing punctuation marks (! ? . , : ; — etc.)
- Different or missing emoji/icons (⚠️ vs ⚠, 👑 vs crown-icon, ⭐ etc. — all variations OK)
- Unicode variation selectors (⚠ ≡ ⚠️, ❗ ≡ ❗️)
- Different brackets or quote styles ([ ] vs ( ), "" vs «» vs '')
- Different number formatting (99.999 vs 99,999 vs 99 999)
- Extra or missing spaces, line breaks
- Diacritics/accents variations that look identical visually
- Minor 1-letter typos in long words where the word is still readable

ONLY fail text_matches if actual letters/words are WRONG, MISSING, or SCRAMBLED (garbled typos, missing key words, wrong language).

text_readable=true if the text is legible (even if slightly stylized).
text_artifacts=true ONLY if there are clearly corrupt/gibberish characters (not minor stylistic differences).
composition_ok=true for any reasonable layout.
overall_pass=true if text_matches AND text_readable (ignore text_artifacts for minor style variations).

Return ONLY JSON:
{
  "text_readable": true/false,
  "text_matches": true/false,
  "text_artifacts": true/false,
  "composition_ok": true/false,
  "overall_pass": true/false,
  "issues": "only describe MAJOR issues (wrong words, gibberish), not minor style differences"
}
adapt_text_system_template:
Video title (context only, do NOT add it to output): {video_title}

You will receive the TEXT ON THE COVER (not the video title). Adapt ONLY that cover text into {target_language} natively.

RULES:
1. Do NOT add words from the video title — adapt ONLY what was on the cover.
2. Do NOT translate word for word — adapt so it sounds natural and catchy.
3. Preserve the TRIGGER — the emotional hook that makes viewers click.
4. Keep length (±20%) — never longer than original.
5. PRESERVE STRUCTURE: if the cover has separate labels on different lines, KEEP line breaks (\n). Do NOT merge into one sentence.
6. Keep numbers, money, percentages, counters, and universal symbols AS-IS (e.g. $10,000, 99%, *99, SSS-RANK).
7. Keep emojis and special symbols (⚠️ 👑 ❗ 💥) exactly as they are.
8. Prefer short words — long translations can cause rendering issues in the generation model.

Return ONLY the adapted cover text (keep line breaks and separators from source), nothing else.
generation_prompt_template:
YouTube thumbnail, 16:9 aspect ratio, high contrast, vivid colors.

COMPOSITION & SUBJECT (PRIMARY DIRECTIVE):
{composition_block}

TEXT ON COVER (render this exactly, NOT the video title, keep line breaks): "{cover_text}"
{text_block}

TEXT STYLE (render exactly as specified, this is a new generated image — not an edit):
- Use the font family, weight and letter case described above.
- Keep the described text layout and line structure: line breaks, number of labels and their relative positions.

{video_title_line}{mood} mood, high quality, cinematic.

Scene: {scene}.

Main characters and objects must be clearly visible.

PRESERVE the art style of the reference (drawing style, linework, shading, color grading, rendering medium). If reference is illustrated — keep illustrated. If cel-shaded — keep cel-shaded. If photo-realistic — keep photo-realistic.

{style_prompt} {style_suffix} {colors}

CRITICAL TEXT RULES:
- ALL text on the image must be ONLY in the target language. Do NOT keep any text from the original/reference image. Do NOT mix languages.
- Replace every word, label, sign, and inscription with the target-language version.
- The ONLY text allowed on the image is: "{cover_text}".
- Text must be bold, high-contrast, readable at small preview sizes.
- Do NOT write the video title on the image.
simple_edit_prompt_template:
You are editing an existing YouTube thumbnail (the attached image). Create an ORIGINAL variation of it, not a 1:1 copy.

DO:
- Translate ALL text, labels and numbers on the thumbnail into {language}. Keep them bold, high-contrast and readable at small preview sizes; keep roughly the same position, size and layout as in the original.
- Slightly change the characters' poses, facial expressions and camera angle so it looks like a fresh, original cover.
- Keep the SAME art style, rendering, color palette, characters and overall composition as the original.

DON'T:
- Do NOT keep any text in the original language — every word must be in {language}.
- Do NOT add watermarks, logos or extra text that was not there.
- Do NOT copy the original pixel-for-pixel.

Output a single 16:9 YouTube thumbnail image.
simple_check_prompt_template:
You are given TWO YouTube thumbnails. The FIRST image is the ORIGINAL. The SECOND image is a generated version whose text should be the ORIGINAL text translated into {language}.

Check the SECOND image against the FIRST. You are a LENIENT reviewer — pass on minor differences (case, punctuation, emoji, spacing, small stylistic changes). Only fail for real problems.

Return ONLY JSON (no markdown):
{
  "text_readable": true/false,
  "text_in_target_language": true/false,
  "text_matches_meaning": true/false,
  "text_artifacts": true/false,
  "overall_pass": true/false,
  "issues": "only MAJOR issues (wrong language, gibberish, wrong meaning); empty string if fine"
}

Rules:
- text_readable = the text on the 2nd image is legible.
- text_in_target_language = the text is in {language}, not in the original language.
- text_matches_meaning = the 2nd image conveys the same message as the 1st, correctly translated.
- text_artifacts = there are clearly corrupt or gibberish characters.
- overall_pass = text_readable AND text_in_target_language AND text_matches_meaning AND NOT text_artifacts.
style_ref_prompt_template: Completely redraw the first image as a NEW original YouTube thumbnail in the exact art style of the second image (same rendering, brushwork, font, colors, lighting, mood). Keep the first image's subject and meaning, but change the poses, angle and composition so it's not a copy. Translate all text into {language}. Use the second image ONLY for style — never its objects, scene or text. Output one 16:9 thumbnail.
